Replace each `___` with code, remove `#| eval: false` and run the chunk. Write your answer under each chunk.

The data are all flights that departed from New York in 2013. They come from the `nycflights13` package.

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(
  here,            # file paths that work on any computer
  tidyverse,       # ggplot2, dplyr, tidyr and friends
  nycflights13     # all flights departing New York City in 2013
)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
# flights comes from the nycflights13 package, so no csv file is needed
flights <- nycflights13::flights
```

## Your turn 1: select a range

Select the columns from `dep_time` to `arr_delay`.

```{r}
#| label: turn-1a
flights |>
  select(dep_time:arr_delay)
```

Answer: 6 columns.

Select all columns except `dep_time` to `arr_delay`.

```{r}
#| label: turn-1b
flights |>
  select(!dep_time:arr_delay)
```

Answer: 13 columns.

## Your turn 2: select by pattern

Select the columns that end in `time`.

```{r}
#| label: turn-2a
flights |>
  select(ends_with("time"))
```

Answer: 5 columns.

Select the columns that start with `sched`.

```{r}
#| label: turn-2b
#| eval: false
flights |>
  select(starts_with("sched"))
```

Answer: [YOUR ANSWER HERE] columns.

## Your turn 3: AND and OR

Flights that departed on December 25.

```{r}
#| label: turn-3a
flights |>
  filter(month == 12 & day == 25) |>
  filter(dep_delay > 0)
```

Flights that departed in June or July, with `|`.

```{r}
#| label: turn-3b
flights |>
  filter(month == 6 | month == 7) |>
  filter(origin == "JFK")
```

The same flights as the previous question, with `%in%`.

```{r}
#| label: turn-3c
flights |>
  filter(month %in% c(6, 7))
```

Answer: both versions return 57,668 rows. Check it with `count()`.

## Your turn 4: NOT

Flights that did not depart from JFK.

```{r}
#| label: turn-4a
flights |>
  filter(origin != "JFK") |>
  count(origin)
```

Answer: 2 airports remain.

Flights that did not depart from JFK or LGA.

```{r}
#| label: turn-4b
flights |>
  filter(!(origin %in% c("JFK", "LGA"))) |>
  count(origin)
```

Answer: EWR is the only airport left.

## See the distribution of dep delay from JFK in Christmas time

Delay in minutes.

```{r}
#| label: jfk-christmas-delays-minutes
flights |>
  filter(origin == "JFK") |>             # this is the airport
  filter(month == 12 & day == 25) |>     # this is Christmas Day
  filter(!is.na(dep_delay)) |>           # drop flights with no delay recorded
  ggplot(aes(x = dep_delay)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, fill = "#2adb4d", color = "white") +   # 10-minute bars
  labs(
    title = "Departure delays from JFK on December 25, 2013",
    x = "Departure delay (minutes)",
    y = "Number of flights"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Delay in hours.

```{r}
#| label: jfk-christmas-delays-hours
flights |>
  filter(origin == "JFK") |>             # this is the airport
  filter(month == 12 & day == 25) |>     # this is Christmas Day
  filter(!is.na(dep_delay)) |>           # drop flights with no delay recorded
  mutate(dep_delay_hours = dep_delay / 60) |>   # minutes to hours
  ggplot(aes(x = dep_delay_hours)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, fill = "#2adb4d", color = "white") +   # 15-minute bars
  labs(
    title = "Departure delays from JFK on December 25, 2013",
    x = "Departure delay (hours)",
    y = "Number of flights"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Only flights with a delay of less than 1 hour.

```{r}
#| label: jfk-christmas-delays-under-1h
flights |>
  filter(origin == "JFK") |>             # this is the airport
  filter(month == 12 & day == 25) |>     # this is Christmas Day
  filter(!is.na(dep_delay)) |>           # drop flights with no delay recorded
  mutate(dep_delay_hours = dep_delay / 60) |>   # minutes to hours
  filter(dep_delay_hours < 1) |>         # keep delays under 1 hour
  ggplot(aes(x = dep_delay_hours)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1 / 12, fill = "#2adb4d", color = "white") +   # 5-minute bars
  labs(
    title = "Departure delays under 1 hour from JFK on December 25, 2013",
    x = "Departure delay (hours)",
    y = "Number of flights"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Pivot

```{r}
#| label: load-gapminder
# Life expectancy by country and year, read straight from a Google Sheet
gapminder_wide <- read_csv("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vQMKvrshkL1R55vcnXnXQ14VfJM6HB62bed8U6ukVc-9ncRg79co2GoaS84eb1o4aEg1bqLFiWNJAS3/pub?gid=554197504&single=true&output=csv")
```
# EDA


```{r}
#| label: view-gapminder
#| eval: false
# View() opens the table in a spreadsheet-like tab. It only works when you run the cell, not when you render
#View(gapminder_wide)
```

# Data manipulation

```{r}
#| label: baltic-select
gapminder_wide |>
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>   # the three Baltic countries
  select(geo, name, "1980":"2026")                           # every year from 1980 to 2026
```



## The plot

```{r}
#| label: pivot-plot
gapminder_wide |>
  # filter and select
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>
  select(geo, name, "1880":"2026") |>    # keep name for the legend
  # pivot: the year columns become one year column and one life_exp column
  pivot_longer(
    cols = "1880":"2026",
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "life_exp"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = year,
    y = life_exp,
    group = geo,                         # connect the points of each country into one line
    color = name                         # one color per country
  )) +
  geom_line()
```

## The plot after WWII

The Second World War ended in 1945, so this plot starts in 1946.

```{r}
#| label: pivot-plot-after-wwii
gapminder_wide |>
  # filter and select
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>
  select(geo, name, "1946":"2026") |>    # only the years after WWII
  # pivot: the year columns become one year column and one life_exp column
  pivot_longer(
    cols = "1946":"2026",
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "life_exp"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = year,
    y = life_exp,
    group = geo,                         # connect the points of each country into one line
    color = name                         # one color per country
  )) +
  geom_line()
```

# Long to wide


```{r}
table2
```

```{r}
#| label: table2-wider
table2 |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = type,                   # the values of type become new column names
    values_from = count                  # the values of count fill the new columns
  ) |>
  mutate(year = as.factor(year)) |>      # year as a category: the axis shows only 1999 and 2000
  # adjust by 100,000 population
  mutate(case_per_100000 = (cases / population) * 100000) |>

  # the plot
  ggplot(aes(
    x = year,
    y = case_per_100000,                 # cases per 100,000 people
    color = country,                     # one color per country
    group = country                      # connect the points of each country into one line
  )) +
  # scale_y_log10() +
  geom_line()
```
